model_name: Microsoft Entra ID Cloud Incident Response Rules

repeated_failed_signins.description: Three or more failed sign-ins from the same source occur within five minutes.

success_after_failures.description: Successful authentication occurs from the same source shortly after repeated failures.

high_signin_risk.description: The successful sign-in is marked as high risk.

unmanaged_device.description: The successful session originates from an unmanaged device.

noncompliant_device.description: The successful session originates from a noncompliant device.

unfamiliar_external_source.description: Authentication originates from an unfamiliar external source rather than the established internal baseline.

report_only_policy_failure.description: A report-only Conditional Access policy would have failed for the observed session.

mfa_satisfied_reduction.description: MFA was successfully satisfied, reducing confidence in an MFA-bypass hypothesis.

enabled_policy_blocked.description: An enabled Conditional Access policy blocked the sign-in; preserve as defensive-control evidence rather than compromise evidence.

role_added_without_justification.description: Cloud role access was added without documented business justification.

role_modified_without_ticket.description: Cloud role assignment was modified without an associated change or incident ticket.

suspicious_session_role_activity.description: Privilege activity occurred within the suspicious authenticated session.

approved_pim_activity_reduction.description: Privileged activity used an approved PIM-style workflow with documented justification and ticketing.

sensitive_document_access.description: The suspicious session accessed sensitive Finance content.

cloud_resource_enumeration.description: The session enumerated cloud data or resource configuration.

vm_login_access_requested.description: The suspicious session requested access to log in to a Finance virtual machine.

multiple_cloud_services.description: The same suspicious session accessed multiple cloud services.

single_identity_multiple_services.description: One identity performed suspicious activity across multiple cloud services.

separate_dormant_identity_activity.description: A separate dormant identity generated suspicious authentication, privilege, and resource activity.

session_revoked.description: Active sessions were revoked as a containment action.

role_removed.description: Suspicious privileged access was removed during containment.

account_disabled.description: The affected identity was disabled during containment.

incident_classification.description: The model prioritizes suspicious cloud activity for investigation without automatically declaring credential theft or account compromise as confirmed.

finance_identity: Revoke active sessions for the affected Finance identity.
Review and remove unauthorized cloud role assignments.
Review Microsoft 365 and Azure resource activity associated with the suspicious session.
Review access to Finance documents and storage objects.
Review VM access attempts and role changes.
Preserve Entra ID sign-in, Conditional Access, PIM, and Azure activity logs.
Reset credentials if additional compromise evidence supports that action.
dormant_identity: Review resources accessed during the dormant-account session.
Investigate how the dormant identity became active.
Preserve related Entra ID and Azure audit evidence.

analyst_guardrails: Do not classify repeated failed sign-ins followed by success as confirmed credential theft without additional evidence.
Do not classify MFA as bypassed when telemetry shows MFA was satisfied.
Do not treat a report-only Conditional Access failure as an actively blocked sign-in.
Do not classify cloud role assignment as confirmed privilege escalation unless the mechanism and authorization context are established.
Do not classify document or blob access as confirmed data exfiltration without evidence that data left the controlled environment.
Do not classify a VM login access request as successful VM compromise.
Separate incident activity from later containment and response actions.
Distinguish confirmed observations from analyst hypotheses.
